control_non_monday_tuesday: First versions carry rows on every other run date in the window (1.0 to 36.6 MB at first landing). Read from the version listing: 2026-10-11 Sunday first version 1753992 bytes with 6278 data rows; 2026-10-14 Wednesday first version 798508 bytes with 2921 data rows; 2026-10-08 Thursday 32839968 bytes with 119967 data rows; 2026-10-07 Wednesday 18669454 bytes with 68620 data rows.
window_rule: data/cot/scripts/bronze/cot_bronze_ingest.py at 33b647a50f (byte-equal to the deployed shared module). transactions is not in SNAPSHOT_TABLES (:147), so the as-of lag in _as_of_for (:302-308, the test at :306) does not apply and the end date is run_date. TABLE_DATE_MODE transactions = Custom, 14 (:131). _window_for_asof sets start = end - 14 (:320-321); _window_for (:327-335) returns that for run_date. The deployed env BD_TXN_CHUNK_DAYS=3 (set by commit bd44c6b010) makes ingest_table (:797-798) call _ingest_transactions_chunked, which tiles the window newest-first into 3-day chunks (_chunk_windows :338-362). The newest chunk is [run_date-2, run_date] and lands as TRANSACTIONS_DAILY_<run_date> (:811-821, land at :897). The caller is infra/aws/lambda/bd-pipeline/bd-49f-runner/lambda_function.py: :236 start,end = mod._window_for(table, run_date); :244 mod.ingest_table(...). Result: a Monday run asks for 2026-10-10..2026-10-12 (Sat to Mon; event 399576550229). A Tuesday run asks for 2026-10-11..2026-10-13 (Sun to Tue; event 399595818161). A Wednesday run asks Mon to Wed (2026-10-12..10-14) and a Thursday run asks Tue to Thu.
window_as_of_measured: Return Date column of the first version (BD as-of): Sunday 2026-10-11 file as-of Fri 10-09 (6264 rows dated 10-09); Wednesday 2026-10-07 as-of Mon 10-05 (no 10-06 rows); Thursday 2026-10-08 as-of Tue 10-06 (119944 rows dated 10-06); Wednesday 2026-10-14 as-of Mon 10-12 (2804 rows dated 10-12, none dated 10-13). Monday and Tuesday as-of values are not read directly; they are inferred from these neighbours. The Tuesday file (2026-10-13) is header-only while its span holds Monday, so Monday was not yet published at 00:02Z.
cause_evidence: BD publishes the trade date only after the run's 00:00Z start: the 00:00Z run's data ends at the last published business day (measured: Friday on the Sunday run, Monday on the Wednesday run; inferred: Friday on the Monday and Tuesday runs). The newest chunk covers only the run date and the two days before it, so a file is non-empty exactly when that span reaches the last published day; Monday's span (Sat-Mon) and Tuesday's span (Sun-Tue) do not, and the same request shape returns rows on every other weekday. The vendor is not the cause, because the window asks for days with no published trades, and the runner builds the request as its code states.
later_cell_would: A later cell would anchor the newest transactions chunk to the last published business day (extend the as-of lag at cot_bronze_ingest.py:306 to transactions, or floor the newest chunk start at that day), re-land and re-emit the ten Monday and Tuesday dates, and decide whether a measured-empty transactions window may complete a day (runner EMPTY_WINDOW_OK_TABLES, :118). Named, not made.
sentinel_content_note: The post-deploy runner accepts a measured-empty transactions export as complete (:118, :137, :163). So the 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13 sentinels exist and are honest about their existence, but their transactions table holds no rows. Whether silver for those two dates was built on that content is not read in this cell.
